findings.title: Adding required profile fields breaks production `build_profiles()`; no task updates it
findings.description: Task 2.1 adds two *required* fields to `BehavioralProfile`, but task 2.2 is explicitly scoped to "all `BehavioralProfile` call sites **in tests**". `src/migratory_server/simulation.py:18-25` (`build_profiles()`) constructs `BehavioralProfile` from `ProfileConfig` with only the six existing fields, so after 2.1 it raises `TypeError`. It is called unconditionally at `src/migratory_server/server.py:71`, and `config/default.yaml` contains a `profiles` section, so this breaks `tests/test_simulation.py:27-42` (`TestBuildProfiles`), `tests/test_server.py:232` (`test_entities_spawned_from_config`), `tests/test_main.py:69` (`test_starts_with_default_config`), and server startup itself. The catch-all in 2.2 ("search across `tests/`") cannot fix source code, so the 2.2 verify step ("all existing tests still pass"), 6.1, and Verification Walkthrough step 1 ("all tests green") are unreachable as written, and the 2.3/6.3 commits would commit a broken repo. A task is needed to thread the new values through `ProfileConfig` (`src/migratory_server/config.py:51-60`) and `build_profiles()` — and it must say where the values come from, since CLAUDE.md forbids silent fallback values (hardcoded `0.0` would violate project conventions).

findings.title: `spawn_population()` bypasses the new leadership array
findings.description: Task 1.1 adds `leadership` to `AgentState.create()`, `add_agent()`, and `remove_agent()`, but `EntityManager.spawn_population()` builds a batch at `src/migratory_server/entities.py:122` and then manually concatenates only positions, velocities, accelerations, and profile_indices — leaving `self._state.leadership` at the zero-length array from `EntityManager.__init__`. Task 1.2 explicitly asserts other call sites "use `AgentState.create()` so they should work without changes", which is false for this path: `state.count` (derived from positions) diverges from `leadership.shape[0]`, `remove_entity()` would `np.delete` past the end of that array, and `LeadershipForce`'s `state.leadership[neighbors]` indexing would fail for any server-spawned population. This leaves the design's `AgentState` extension only partially delivered (the Integration Points section promises the array is available to slices 103/104/107). Add a step extending the merge, and replace the incorrect no-op claim in 1.2.

findings.title: Vectorization Technical Requirement has no task, and 4.1's formula contradicts it
findings.description: Slice design line 395-396 requires "Both forces are vectorized within each agent's neighborhood — no nested Python loops". No step in 3.1 or 4.1 states or verifies this, unlike slice 101's tasks 2.1/3.1/4.1 which each had an explicit "Use vectorized NumPy within each neighborhood — no `for neighbor in neighbors` inner loop" step. Worse, 4.1 specifies `sum(velocity[i] * leadership[i]) / sum(leadership)` and 3.1 says "For each active agent: compute speed…", which a junior AI would naturally implement as a scalar per-neighbor Python loop. There is no test or verification step that would catch this, so the Technical Requirement has no corresponding task. Add an explicit vectorization instruction plus a verification step to 3.1/4.1 (or a test in 3.2/4.2).

findings.title: Overweight verification and integration sections — name what to cut or merge
findings.description: Sections 5–6 contain work beyond what the success criteria need. Task 6.2 repeats the `isinstance(..., BulkForce)` assertions already required by 3.1, 3.2, 4.1, and 4.2 — pure duplication. Task 5.3 re-runs the same seeded 50-agent / 300-tick simulation from 5.2 with a control profile, even though Verification Walkthrough step 5 says "The herding convergence check implicitly tests this"; its assertion is also an ambiguous disjunction ("variance < … **or** mean eastward > …") rather than a single measurable metric. Task 5.1's "confirm forces interact correctly" specifies no assertion at all. Merge 5.3's control-run comparison into 5.2 as one comparison test (this still satisfies the profile-differentiation Technical Requirement), fold 5.1's smoke check into 5.2, and delete 6.2 (fold into 6.1). Also drop 1.2's no-op "should work without changes, but verify" substep in favour of the real production call-site work from the finding above. The rest of the file (one task file, six sections, 18 tasks) is proportionate to this medium-effort slice.

findings.title: Stale test-count baseline in Context Summary and 6.1
findings.description: Task 6.1 says "All tests pass (existing 80 + new herding tests)" and the frontmatter/Context Summary claim "80 tests passing". The repo now contains roughly 230 test functions across 15 test files, including the completed 300–303 world-server slices. The criterion "all tests pass" is correct, but the baseline number and the projectState (which omits the server slices entirely) are stale and could mislead a junior AI into thinking the suite is unexpectedly large or that tests are missing.

findings.title: Functional success criteria are covered with no scope creep
findings.description: Every functional/technical criterion maps to a task: `BulkForce` conformance (3.1/3.2/4.1/4.2), hand-constructed inputs (3.2/4.2), no-neighbor zero (4.1/4.2), stationary zero (3.1/3.2), all-zero-leadership zero plus the epsilon guard matching the Risk Assessment mitigation (4.1/4.2), `active_indices` isolation (3.1/4.1 + 3.2/4.2), self-exclusion and own-leadership-does-not-affect-self (4.1/4.2), uniform-leadership degradation (4.2), five-force `tick()` with leaders (5.1/5.2), directional bias (5.2), profile differentiation (5.3), required profile fields with no new validation (2.1), per-agent `leadership` array with `create`/`add_agent`/`remove_agent` (1.1/1.2), and stateless Option-A momentum that ignores `neighbor_lists` (3.1). Verification Walkthrough steps 2 and 3 are reproduced as unit tests in 3.2/4.2. I found no task that fails to trace to a design element.

findings.title: Sequencing, test-with pattern, and commit checkpoints
findings.description: Dependencies are respected and acyclic: state and profile extensions precede the forces; `herding.py` is created in 3.1 before 4.1 adds to it; integration tests in Section 5 follow both forces; final verification is last. Each implementation task is immediately followed by its test task (1.1→1.2, 2.1→2.2, 3.1→3.2, 4.1→4.2). Commit checkpoints (1.3, 2.3, 3.3, 4.3, 5.4) sit after implementation+test pairs, i.e. working tested points, not after every single task. The file uses checkbox-based "**N.N Commit:**" items rather than plain `**Commit**:` lines; a file with no plain markers is acceptable, and the checkbox form matches CLAUDE.md's "Use checklist format for all task files". No load-test or CI-gating task is required here: the slice design restates no quantitative NFR (the "no nested Python loops" item is an implementation-shape requirement, not a load-testable target), and no `tests/load/` exists.
